items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-15
items.q: I remember hearing the, the, uh, the music from a distance, just hearing, uh, bunk and baby as I, I guess, uh, crossed the street.

ctx.x: or any kind of perspective. That's right. They really, that thinking is very much out of date. That's my belief, anyway. I'll have to put some of myself in there. One thing that interested me was... your description of the first time you ever came to the Stuyvesant, and you're approaching the place. Yeah.

What was the lie? Yeah, well, uh... first time I came, I was very young and kind of scared. It was the first time I was in a strange city by myself and, and, uh... I had received some kind of garbled directions of how to get at the Stuyvesant. And, uh, somehow I managed to... to get that, what was it? Second Avenue, I think it was on. But, uh... I remember, you know, wondering if I would ever find the place. And if I didn't, what would I do, you know? And, uh... Uh... I remember hearing the, the, uh, the music…
Well, that, by... My standards of present day New Orleans, that's not very loud, you know?

items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: And I guess I get Bunk actually had trouble with both drummers, Baby and Steel.

ctx.x: That second engagement, if I remember rightly, was the only one when Maude was up there, too. There was something you were telling the other night, the time when Maude was at the table. I forget what the story is now, but you were there once when she was there in New York, too.

Yeah, well, I was telling a couple stories the other night, happening to be at the Stuyvesant when there was conflict in the band, when Bunk was having trouble with a drummer. And I guess I get Bunk actually had trouble with both drummers, Baby and Steel.
I know, even Kaiser Marshall, too.
